modules.description: A virtual machine in the WB cloud: provision a batch, tear one down, resize it, or read the inventory.
modules.name: vm

created.description:
Provision `count` VMs and wait until every one of them is ready.
Idempotent on the batch identity: a rerun adopts the live VMs it already
made (matched by the cloud label `soulstack-run`, or by the name
`<name>-<seq>` for VMs made before the label existed) and tops up only
what is missing, at the first free indexes.
Output.hosts is the provisioned batch, one entry per VM:
{sid, vm_id, primary_ip, external_ip, attributes}. It does NOT carry
bootstrap_token — minting one needs the Keeper's token store, which a
plugin has no access to (NIM-757, see README).
No dry-run preview.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM CA certificate that verifies the WB endpoint. Absent, the connection is plaintext (WB's :80 default). Masked (secret).

client_cert_pem.description: PEM client certificate for mTLS to the WB endpoint (only together with client_key_pem). Masked (secret).

client_key_pem.description: PEM client key for mTLS to the WB endpoint (only together with client_cert_pem). Masked (secret); does not end up in events or errors.

count.description: How many VMs the batch holds. The scan counts what already exists, so this is the TOTAL, not the number to add.

endpoint.description: WB compute gRPC endpoint, host:port — e.g. grpc.clv3:80. Plaintext unless a CA is supplied.

key_id.description: WB API-key id. Exchanged for a short-lived access token on every call; not itself a bearer credential, so it is not masked.

name.description: Batch identity: VMs are named `<name>-<seq>` and labelled with it. Required unless profile.labels["soulstack-run"] is set — without one of the two a rerun cannot recognise its own VMs and would spawn orphans.

namespace.description: WB namespace the VMs live in. The placement fallback for `created` (profile.namespace wins) and the only source for the other actions. One of namespace / namespace_id is required.

namespace_id.description: WB namespace id, the alternative spelling of `namespace`.

profile.description: The VM spec: namespace XOR namespace_id, network_id (UUID), cpu_size (cores), ram_size and boot_disk_size (BYTES), rm_external_id (Resource Manager id of the owning system — cmdb_system_id as a string, or the legacy numeric id; WB REFUSES a create without it), and the image as EITHER image_id (exact UUID) OR image_name (e.g. debian-12, resolved against the image list; optional image_version pins one when a name carries several). Plus the optional boot_disk_name / set_external_ip / external_ip_id / anti_affinity / cluster / deletion_protection / labels. Checked in Validate — see the README for the field table.

secret.description: WB API-key secret (vault-ref in operator input; keeper resolves it before Apply). Masked in logs/traces/UI.

userdata.description: cloud-init user-data, at most 32 KiB (WB's declared ci_user_data max_len; an overflow is refused before the API call). NOTE: WB rejects the field outright for a key that is not allowed to use it.

destroyed.description:
Delete every VM in `vm_ids` and CONFIRM the teardown by polling.
WB's delete is asynchronous — a successful call means "accepted" — and it
can also be REFUSED outright: a VM that is still creating answers
FailedPrecondition "still being created" and keeps running. Either way the
delete is re-issued until the teardown is confirmed. A teardown that could
not be confirmed is reported failed, with the vm_id, never as success.
No dry-run preview.

vm_ids.description: WB VM ids to tear down. A VM that is already gone is an idempotent success.

probed.description:
Read the VM inventory of a namespace. Read-only, changed=false by
design (a probe, not a mutation): it creates, deletes and modifies
nothing. Output.hosts has the same shape `created` produces, so a
reconnaissance step and a provision step are read the same way.
No dry-run preview.

run_label.description: Report only VMs carrying this value in the cloud label `soulstack-run` — the batch identity `created` stamps. Ignored when vm_ids is set.

vm_ids.description: Report only these VM ids. Omitted, the whole namespace is listed (optionally narrowed by run_label).

resized.description:
Resize every VM in `vm_ids` to an ABSOLUTE target.
Disk grows online through the disk service (never shrinks — a target at or
below the current size is an idempotent skip). cpu/ram go through
stop → update → start and therefore need allow_downtime.
The namespace quota remainder is prechecked against the batch's summed
positive delta: it fails closed, before any VM is touched.
No dry-run preview.

allow_downtime.description: EXPLICIT consent to stop and start the VM. Required for a cpu/ram change and refused up front without it, so a batch never ends up half-stopped. A disk-only resize is online and does not need it.

client_key_pem.description: PEM client key for mTLS to the WB endpoint (only together with client_cert_pem). Masked (secret); does not end up in events or errors.

cpu_cores.description: Target vCPU count. 0 leaves cpu alone.

disk_gb.description: Target boot-disk size in GiB (converted to the bytes WB expects). 0 leaves the disk alone. Shrinking is refused as an idempotent skip.

endpoint.description: WB compute gRPC endpoint, host:port — e.g. grpc.clv3:80. Plaintext unless a CA is supplied.

key_id.description: WB API-key id. Exchanged for a short-lived access token on every call; not itself a bearer credential, so it is not masked.

namespace_id.description: WB namespace id, the alternative spelling of `namespace`.

ram_mb.description: Target RAM in MiB (converted to the bytes WB expects). 0 leaves ram alone.

secret.description: WB API-key secret (vault-ref in operator input; keeper resolves it before Apply). Masked in logs/traces/UI.

vm_ids.description: WB VM ids to resize. Every VM in the batch gets the same target.
